title: Best AI-Native ATS for Recruitment Agencies (2026): Built-In AI vs Bolted-On
summary: Stardex separates AI-native recruiting platforms from legacy ATS with bolted-on AI and ranks the 2026 options for agencies by automation depth and data model.
body_markdown:
Compare Stardex and five AI ATS alternatives for recruitment agencies in 2026, including built-in AI depth, workflow actions, pricing, and buying trade-offs.


Recruiting intelligence buried in notes, emails, and calls is difficult to retrieve when a new search starts. We compare Stardex, Recruiterflow, Loxo, Recruit CRM, Manatal, and Bullhorn on built-in AI depth, record updates, executable actions, and pricing, not generic ATS features. Our first editorial recommendation for agencies combining contingent recruiting with retained or executive search is Stardex. Using official documentation reviewed as of October 21, 2026 (not hands-on testing), we treat “AI-native” as an editorial framework for documented workflow depth, not a certified architecture classification or a label inferred from product age or packaging.


## **Why do recruitment agencies need an AI-native ATS?**


Recruitment agencies need more than a place to store candidate information: they need to retrieve relationship context, maintain records, and act on that information within appropriate controls. Capturing a conversation does not automatically make its details searchable or update the fields recruiters use. Likewise, generating an outreach draft is different from executing a workflow action. At Stardex, we describe our ATS + CRM as AI-native because AI is integrated into these recruiting workflows. The practical test is what the system can retrieve, update, and execute—not simply whether it includes a chatbot.


### **Which recruiting problems create the need for an AI-native ATS?**


-


**Buried relationship context.** Relevant candidate information can sit in notes, emails, and transcripts rather than structured fields. Our[semantic search](https://www.stardex.com/) spans those sources alongside candidate records, helping recruiters retrieve context from existing relationships.


-


**Conversation details not reflected in fields.** Recording a call and maintaining a record are separate capabilities.[Stardex AI Notetaker](https://www.stardex.com/integrations/ai-notetaker) associates recordings, transcripts, and summaries with attendee records; transcript-based AI field updates are[documented separately](https://www.stardex.com/pricing) . Buyers should verify both capture and write-back rather than assume one includes the other.


-


**Changing candidate information.** A stored company or title can become outdated.[Profile Refresh](https://www.stardex.com/integrations/profile-refresh) checks selected candidate and contact records on a configurable schedule, using purchased credits to retrieve available updates from data providers. This is provider-dependent enrichment, not guaranteed real-time detection of every job change.


-


**Disconnected workflow execution.** Producing text is not the same as updating a recruiting record. Our[MCP server](https://www.stardex.com/integrations/mcp) gives compatible AI clients tools for searches and controlled writes. Updates depend on available tools, authenticated-user permissions, and client approval behavior; our documentation recommends testing read-only lookups first.


Stardex connects these needs through semantic retrieval, conversation capture, separately documented transcript-to-field updates, scheduled profile enrichment, and permission-controlled agent tools. That gives agencies concrete capabilities to evaluate rather than an architectural label to accept at face value. Several alternatives also provide substantive integrated AI, so the comparison should focus on demonstrated workflows, not a blanket native-versus-legacy judgment. For a 2026 evaluation, ask vendors to demonstrate retrieval, record maintenance, and controlled actions using representative recruiting information. Recruiters should retain responsibility for assessing candidate relevance and deciding how to proceed.


## **What should recruitment firms look for in an AI-native ATS?**


Evaluate AI where recruiting work actually happens: retrieving candidate context, updating records after conversations, and taking controlled actions. A useful demo should follow information from a call through to a saved record and a subsequent search—not stop at a generated summary. At Stardex, we describe our platform as an AI-native ATS and CRM, but that positioning should still be tested against documented functionality. For your 2026 shortlist, use the five criteria below to examine database reuse, administrative work, and support for both contingent and retained searches.


### **Which five AI-native ATS capabilities should agencies evaluate?**


-


**Unstructured-context retrieval.** Ask which profiles, notes, emails, and transcripts are searchable, and whether retrieval uses semantic search, full-text search, or natural-language-to-Boolean translation. These are different capabilities; test each against an actual search brief. We document[semantic search across candidate records, notes, emails, and transcripts](https://www.stardex.com/) , giving agencies a concrete scope to evaluate rather than relying on an “AI search” label.


-


**Conversation-to-record write-back.** Distinguish a recording from a summary, a proposed update, and a saved field change. Ask the vendor to demonstrate what reaches the candidate record and where recruiter review occurs. Stardex’s[Starter plan documents transcript-based AI field updates](https://www.stardex.com/pricing) , alongside automatic tagging and summaries-specific functions to inspect when assessing post-call administration.


-


**Executable, permission-controlled actions.** Check available tools, authenticated-user permissions, and the connected AI client’s approval behavior. Our[remote MCP server](https://www.stardex.com/integrations/mcp) supports recruiting-entity searches and controlled writes, subject to those conditions; our documentation recommends testing read-only lookups first. MCP availability demonstrates agent connectivity, but alone does not establish AI-native architecture or unrestricted authority to change records.


-


**Agency workflow coverage and data maintenance.** Test contingent and retained workflows, candidate matching, outreach, and company relationship intelligence. Stardex supports contingent recruiting and executive search; our[AI Company Insights](https://www.stardex.com/blog/stardex-product-update-19---in-app-ai-assistant-company-insights-scorecards) organizes information from notes and calls at company level. Also inspect refresh cadence:[Profile Refresh](https://www.stardex.com/integrations/profile-refresh) uses purchased credits and multiple providers to check selected records on a configurable schedule—not guarantee real-time detection of every job change.


-


**Plan entitlements, connectivity, and total usage cost.** Request a breakdown of AI tiers, refresh or enrichment credits, APIs, webhooks, and live versus planned integrations. Stardex lists API access and data exports across plans; Pro adds sequences, webhooks, and candidate job matching. Our[integration directory](https://www.stardex.com/integrations) also distinguishes live connections from planned ones and identifies Zoom-transcript and Calendly workflows as Zapier-based. Confirm billing terms rather than assuming every capability is included.


Apply these same criteria to Stardex, Recruiterflow, Loxo, Recruit CRM, Manatal, and Bullhorn. Record what each vendor demonstrates, what its documentation supports, and what remains unknown; an undocumented capability is not automatically an absent one. Separately priced AI does not establish bolted-on architecture, just as all-inclusive AI pricing does not establish native architecture. We recommend asking every vendor—including Stardex—to demonstrate the same recruiting workflow, with permissions and plan entitlements visible, so your decision rests on supported capabilities rather than labels or an assumption that one platform uniquely checks every box.


## **How do recruitment agencies use an AI-native ATS across contingent and retained searches?**


Recruitment agencies can use an AI-native ATS to connect candidate discovery, conversation capture, record maintenance, and search execution. In Stardex, we support both contingent recruiting and executive search, so recruiters can apply existing relationship knowledge to different types of assignments. The practical question is not whether AI can generate a summary; it is whether that information becomes useful in the next search. These six workflows show how our documented capabilities support that process, with recruiters retaining responsibility for evaluation, outreach decisions, and permitted record changes.


1.


**Rediscover candidates from existing relationship knowledge.**


-


**Feature:** Semantic search across candidate records, notes, emails, and transcripts. **Solution:** Search the context accumulated through previous interactions when preparing a new shortlist, rather than relying only on profile fields. **Offering:** Stardex AI search.


2.


**Turn conversations into usable records.**


-


**Feature:** Meeting capture linked to attendee records. **Solution:** Connect a Google or Microsoft calendar so our[AI Notetaker](https://www.stardex.com/integrations/ai-notetaker) can join eligible Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams meetings and associate recordings, transcripts, and summaries with the relevant people. Administrators and users control enablement, calendars, and exclusions. **Offering:** AI Notetaker.


-


**Feature:** Transcript-based AI field updates. **Solution:** Use transcript information to update structured fields, making conversation details usable beyond the meeting summary. This is a separate capability from recording and summarizing meetings. **Offering:** AI field updates, listed on our pricing page in Starter.


3.


**Refresh selected candidate and contact profiles.**


-


**Feature:** Scheduled, provider-dependent enrichment. **Solution:** Select records and configure a refresh cadence to retrieve available changes in company, title, and work history. This helps maintain relationship data without implying real-time detection of every job change. **Offering:**[Profile Refresh](https://www.stardex.com/integrations/profile-refresh) , using purchased refresh credits.


4.


**Support contingent recruiting pipelines.**


-


**Feature:** Bulk candidate operations. **Solution:** Apply supported operations across groups of candidates when managing pipeline-heavy contingent assignments. **Offering:** Stardex’s contingent recruiting workflows.


-


**Feature:** Outreach sequences. **Solution:** Organize candidate engagement across a sequence of messages while keeping outreach decisions with recruiters. **Offering:** Sequences, listed in Pro on our pricing page.


-


**Feature:** Sourcing automation and team analytics. **Solution:** Support sourcing activity and review recruiting activity across the team as contingent pipelines progress. **Offering:** Stardex’s sourcing automation and analytics capabilities.


5.


**Prepare retained or executive searches using company intelligence.**


-


**Feature:** Company-level insights and reusable scorecards. **Solution:** Bring information from notes and calls into financial, funding, team, and culture categories to inform retained-search preparation; use reusable scorecards to structure assessments. **Offering:**[AI Company Insights and scorecards](https://www.stardex.com/blog/stardex-product-update-19---in-app-ai-assistant-company-insights-scorecards) .


6.


**Connect external AI clients under recruiter control.**


-


**Feature:** MCP read lookups. **Solution:** Let compatible clients—including Claude, OpenAI clients, and Manus—search recruiting entities through our remote MCP server. Start by testing read-only lookups before enabling updates. **Offering:**[Stardex MCP](https://www.stardex.com/integrations/mcp) .


-


**Feature:** Permitted write tools. **Solution:** Allow supported record changes only where a tool is available and the authenticated user has permission. Approval behavior also depends on the compatible client; connecting an agent does not grant unrestricted access. **Offering:** Controlled MCP write actions.


For agencies combining contingent and retained work in 2026, the relevance is this workflow coverage: finding relationship context, capturing new information, maintaining records, and applying that knowledge to pipeline execution or deeper search preparation. Stardex brings these capabilities into an ATS + CRM, but individual capabilities also exist in competing products. Evaluate how they connect in your own workflow rather than treating any single feature as proof of AI-native design. Confirm plan availability, refresh-credit requirements, and approval controls before deciding which steps to enable; recruiter judgment remains essential.


## **How do the best AI ATS platforms for recruitment agencies compare?**


For this 2026 comparison, we assess documented AI depth rather than treating an “AI-native” label as proof of architecture. We put Stardex first for consideration by agencies combining contingent and retained search: our documented combination of contextual search, transcript-based field updates, and controlled agent access addresses candidate discovery and ongoing record maintenance. That is a workflow-fit recommendation, not an exclusive-capability claim. Recruiterflow, Loxo, and Recruit CRM also document substantial write-back or agent capabilities. Bullhorn provides an established-platform benchmark with substantive embedded AI—not a system without AI actions.


**Score key:** **U** = unstructured recruiting context; **W** = record write-back; **A** = executable AI actions. Each receives **2** for explicit broad documentation, **1** for bounded or partial evidence, or **0** where not established in reviewed sources. These are **provisional editorial evidence assessments, not hands-on benchmarks** . Scores are not totaled into a market ranking; “not established” does not mean “absent.”


#### **Stardex**


-


**Vendor-described positioning / editorial context:** We describe Stardex as an AI-native ATS + CRM; first consideration here for mixed contingent-and-retained workflows, not an independently audited architectural advantage.


-


**Documented unstructured-context retrieval:** Semantic search across candidate records, notes, emails, and transcripts.


-


**Record write-back:** Transcript-based AI field updates; automatic tagging and summaries.


-


**Executable actions and controls:** MCP supports controlled writes through available tools, authenticated-user permissions, and compatible client approval behavior. Read-only testing is recommended first.


-


**Provisional U/W/A evidence scores:** U2 / W2 / A2


-


**Pricing and usage caveats:** Confirm billing selection and current terms. Copilot is custom-priced; Pro adds sequences, webhooks, and candidate job matching.


#### **Recruiterflow**


-


**Vendor-described positioning / editorial context:** AIRA combines a Talent Graph with purpose-built agents; separate packaging does not establish bolted-on architecture.


-


**Documented unstructured-context retrieval:** Talent Graph incorporates notes, call transcripts, resumes, enrichment, LinkedIn data, and custom fields. AIRA Search is candidate-only.


-


**Record write-back:** Separate field-update agents can update candidate profiles from Notetaker output.


-


**Executable actions and controls:** Purpose-built agents act in pipelines and write to records. AIRA Search itself is read-only.


-


**Provisional U/W/A evidence scores:** U2 / W2 / A2


-


**Pricing and usage caveats:** Search requires the custom-priced AIRA Plan. Confirm current search limits, agent credit allowances, and overages.


#### **Loxo**


-


**Vendor-described positioning / editorial context:** Markets Core as an AI-native ATS + CRM; Professional adds the complete agentic workforce and Data Agents.


-


**Documented unstructured-context retrieval:** Relevance-ranked AI search plus documented full-text search over activity notes and Notetaker transcripts. Full-text retrieval is not proof of semantic reasoning across all conversations.


-


**Record write-back:** Background profile refresh and company-data standardization; duplicate detection recommends merges.


-


**Executable actions and controls:** MCP connectivity; Data Agents perform background work. Duplicate merges require recruiter approval and are reversible; original values remain visible.


-


**Provisional U/W/A evidence scores:** U1 / W2 / A2


-


**Pricing and usage caveats:** Core starts at $149/user/month, billed annually. Professional is demo-priced; verify feature entitlements.


#### **Recruit CRM**


-


**Vendor-described positioning / editorial context:** Documents AI candidate search, contextual matching, and permissioned MCP—not merely text generation.


-


**Documented unstructured-context retrieval:** Natural-language-to-Boolean candidate search covers notes and other candidate information. Contextual matching uses only the latest three notes and three call logs from the previous three months.


-


**Record write-back:** MCP enrichment writes primary results to fields and additional results to notes; activity creation and updates are supported.


-


**Executable actions and controls:** Actions run under the connected user’s identity with granular role-level read/write permissions.


-


**Provisional U/W/A evidence scores:** U1 / W2 / A2


-


**Pricing and usage caveats:** MCP requires Business or above. AI workflows consume credits; confirm allowances and annual/monthly billing before quoting prices.


#### **Manatal**


-


**Vendor-described positioning / editorial context:** Offers semantic/Boolean search and explainable recommendations; not a keyword-only comparator.


-


**Documented unstructured-context retrieval:** Semantic relevance, configurable matching weights, and requirement-level fit analysis. Complete transcript-history retrieval is not established.


-


**Record write-back:** Resume parsing and recruiter-directed bulk tagging or adding candidates to jobs provide bounded evidence; general agent write-back remains unverified.


-


**Executable actions and controls:** Recommendation agents produce shortlists; recruiters can refine requirements and take bulk actions, including emailing. General autonomous execution remains unverified.


-


**Provisional U/W/A evidence scores:** U1 / W1 / A1


-


**Pricing and usage caveats:** Professional starts at $15/user/month annually, with job/candidate limits. AI Copilot and AI Interviewer are listed separately; recommendation features are beta and terms may change.


#### **Bullhorn**


-


**Vendor-described positioning / editorial context:** Established-platform benchmark with substantive embedded AI; avoid assuming every AI feature is a separate add-on.


-


**Documented unstructured-context retrieval:** Amplify uses notes, emails, and calls. Prompt Studio supports selected context, with 1-10 recent matching notes per prompt, not established unrestricted transcript retrieval.


-


**Record write-back:** Transcription extracts record updates; Prompt Studio can add notes and update fields.


-


**Executable actions and controls:** Digital Workers support screening, outreach, and presentations. Recruitment Cloud enrichment provides review/edit/accept/reject controls; do not generalize those controls to every edition.


-


**Provisional U/W/A evidence scores:** U1 / W2 / A2


-


**Pricing and usage caveats:** Small-agency Pro includes search/match, Chat, enrichment, transcription, and automation; Max adds agentic workflows. Both are quote-based. Confirm edition-specific entitlements.


Use these scores to build a demo checklist, not to infer proprietary architecture or guaranteed outcomes. For Stardex, start with our[MCP controls](https://www.stardex.com/integrations/mcp) and[plan documentation](https://www.stardex.com/pricing) , then test your own search-and-update workflow. Compare that with[Recruiterflow’s Search boundaries](https://help.recruiterflow.com/en/articles/15596978-aira-search-faq) ,[Loxo’s Data Agents](https://www.loxo.co/ai-agents/data-agents) , and[Bullhorn’s Prompt Studio limits](https://kb.bullhorn.com/amplify/Content/Amplify/Topics/amplifyPromptStudio.htm) . Ask each vendor to demonstrate retrieval from historical conversations, a proposed record change, and the permissions governing execution. Confirm current plan access and usage charges before choosing; similar evidence scores can still represent different workflows and controls.

Each profile assesses three signals: use of unstructured recruiting context, record write-back, and executable agent actions. Separate AI plans do not, by themselves, establish that a platform’s architecture is bolted on.

### **Recruiterflow**


Recruiterflow offers substantive contextual retrieval and workflow agents through AIRA. Its Talent Graph assembles candidate evidence from notes, Notetaker transcripts, resumes, LinkedIn data, enrichment, and custom fields, supporting qualitative ranking beyond ordinary database filters. Separate purpose-built agents read CRM data, operate within pipelines, and write updates back to records. For agencies evaluating candidate rediscovery alongside operational automation, that combination deserves consideration. The important distinction is between AIRA Search, which is read-only, and the agents that execute updates—not between “real AI” and an assumed chatbot add-on. ([Talent Graph](https://help.recruiterflow.com/en/articles/15597002-glossary-aira-search-key-terms) ,[agents](https://recruiterflow.com/blog/ai-agents-in-recruiterflow/) )


**AI-depth assessment:** Documented contextual candidate retrieval and agent write-back; Search itself does not execute writes.


**Key Features**


-


AIRA Talent Graph and contextual candidate ranking. ([Source](https://help.recruiterflow.com/en/articles/15597002-glossary-aira-search-key-terms) )


-


Purpose-built agents that read CRM data and write back to records. ([Source](https://recruiterflow.com/blog/ai-agents-in-recruiterflow/) )


**Recruitment Agency Offerings**


-


Candidate rediscovery, Notetaker-to-profile updates, and pipeline and task workflows. ([Agents](https://recruiterflow.com/blog/ai-agents-in-recruiterflow/) ,[plan coverage](https://store.recruiterflow.com/pricing) )


**Pricing**


-


Platform displays $149 per user/month; AIRA is custom-priced. Confirm per-run credit allowances and overage terms rather than assuming unlimited agent usage. ([Pricing](https://store.recruiterflow.com/pricing) ,[agent guide](https://recruiterflow.com/blog/ai-agents-in-recruiterflow/) )


**Pros**


-


Contextual ranking uses evidence beyond structured fields, while integrated agents provide a documented path from information capture to record updates.


**Cons / Buying Considerations**


-


AIRA Search is AIRA-plan-only, candidate-only, and read-only; separate agents handle writes. Recheck saved-query and natural-language-result export restrictions, which appear in the documented release. ([Search FAQ](https://help.recruiterflow.com/en/articles/15596978-aira-search-faq) )

For agencies, the evaluation question is how well that bounded context fits their searches—not whether the platform has executable AI capabilities at all. Genuine record write-back and granular permissions support controlled agent use rather than text generation alone.

([Search scope](https://help.recruitcrm.io/en/articles/10752283-how-to-run-a-search-in-recruit-crm-new-ui) ,[matching limits](https://help.recruitcrm.io/en/articles/9647945-ai-job-candidate-matching-in-recruit-crm) )


### **Manatal**


Manatal combines semantic relevance with Boolean controls, customizable recommendations, and requirement-level fit explanations. Its documented recommendation workflow helps recruiters refine requirements, review explainable shortlists, and then take bulk actions such as tagging, emailing, or assigning candidates to jobs. This is more substantial than keyword matching or resume parsing alone. Manatal also lists AI Copilot and AI Interviewer add-ons, so its offering should not be reduced to recommendations. Agencies should distinguish these documented capabilities from unverified claims about complete transcript-history retrieval or general-purpose agent write-back across the system. ([Features](https://www.manatal.com/features/ai-recommendations) ,[recommendation workflow](https://support.manatal.com/docs/ai-candidate-recommendations) ,[plans](https://www.manatal.com/pricing) )


**AI-depth assessment:** Documented semantic matching and recruiter-directed bulk actions; complete conversation-archive retrieval and general agent write-back remain unestablished.


**Key Features**


-


Semantic relevance with Boolean controls, customizable recommendation weighting, and requirement-level fit analysis. ([Source](https://www.manatal.com/features/ai-recommendations) )

## **How were these AI-native ATS platforms evaluated for recruitment agencies?**


We evaluated official vendor product pages, help documentation, pricing pages, and release notes using October 21, 2026 as the reference date. Our provisional editorial scores assess documented evidence of unstructured-context retrieval, record write-back, and executable AI actions—not hands-on benchmarks or independent architecture audits. Vendor descriptions of “AI-native” architecture remain vendor claims. Stardex’s first placement reflects our assessment of its fit for agencies combining contingent and retained search, rather than a unique numerical lead. The rubric below makes those evidence judgments explicit; the proposed demo protocol has not been completed.


#### **U, Unstructured recruiting context**


-


**What is evaluated:** Searchable information types, retrieval method, historical scope, and coverage of candidates, contacts, and other recruiting entities


-


**Score 0:** Not established by reviewed sources


-


**Score 1:** Bounded or partial evidence, such as limited history or entity coverage


-


**Score 2:** Explicit broad documentation of searchable context, retrieval method, historical scope, and entity coverage


#### **W, Record write-back**


-


**What is evaluated:** Summaries versus proposed changes, approved saved updates, and automated record maintenance


-


**Score 0:** Not established by reviewed sources


-


**Score 1:** Bounded or partial evidence, such as summaries or limited field updates


-


**Score 2:** Explicit broad documentation of saved updates, approval behavior, and automated maintenance


#### **A, Executable AI actions**


-


**What is evaluated:** Suggested follow-ups versus tool-based actions, including permissions, approvals, and completed steps


-


**Score 0:** Not established by reviewed sources


-


**Score 1:** Bounded or partial evidence of executable actions or controls


-


**Score 2:** Explicit broad documentation of tool-based actions, permissions, approvals, and execution behavior


These scores are evidence judgments, not certifications. MCP is neither exclusive to Stardex—Recruit CRM also documents MCP-driven write-back—nor sufficient proof of native architecture. Separate AI pricing is not, by itself, proof of bolted-on AI.


Use the same inputs and requested outcomes when demonstrating Stardex, Recruiterflow, Loxo, Recruit CRM, Manatal, and Bullhorn:


1.


**Historical-note retrieval test.** Supply a candidate detail found only in an old note and ask the system to retrieve it with supporting evidence. **Record:** retrieved detail, supporting note or quotation, retrieval method, historical limits, plan entitlements, and usage charges.


2.


**Transcript-update test.** Supply a transcript containing changed availability or salary preferences. Inspect what the system proposes and what it actually saves. **Record:** proposed field changes, saved values, approval behavior, plan entitlements, and usage charges.


3.


**Approved multi-step task test.** Request the same approved recruiting task in every platform-for example, locate a candidate, update availability, and create a follow-up activity. **Record:** completed actions versus suggestions, permission handling, approval prompts, failures or incomplete steps, plan entitlements, and usage charges. Recruiter review remains part of the protocol.

## **What should recruitment firms know about AI-native ATS platforms?**


### **Why do recruitment firms need an AI-native ATS?**


Recruitment firms need connected retrieval, record maintenance, and controlled actions so candidate knowledge can inform ongoing searches rather than remain scattered across conversations. Stardex brings these functions together through semantic search across records and communications, transcript-based field updates, and MCP tools that let compatible AI clients perform permitted actions. For contingent and retained workflows, that means evaluating whether a system can retrieve relevant context, maintain useful records, and support the next recruiting task. Recruiters should retain judgment over candidate suitability and test automation permissions before enabling updates.


### **What is an AI-native ATS for recruitment agencies in 2026?**


For this 2026 comparison, we define an AI-native ATS through three capabilities: searchable unstructured context, AI write-back to records, and executable actions within recruiting workflows. This is our editorial framework, not an industry certification or an independent audit of any vendor’s architecture. Stardex describes a flexible data layer designed to support AI throughout recruitment, alongside semantic search, transcript-based field updates, and controlled MCP actions. Buyers should test those capabilities with representative notes and workflows rather than treating an AI label or chatbot interface as sufficient evidence.


### **What are the best AI-native ATS platforms for recruitment firms?**


Our 2026 shortlist comprises Stardex, Recruiterflow, Loxo, Recruit CRM, Manatal, and Bullhorn, but the right choice depends on demonstrated workflow depth rather than the AI-native label alone. Stardex is our first recommendation for agencies combining contingent recruiting with retained or executive search because we explicitly support both operating models. Recruiterflow documents workflow agents, Loxo documents search and Data Agents, and Recruit CRM documents permissioned MCP writes. Bullhorn provides an established-platform benchmark; evaluate Manatal against the same tests before deciding.


### **Which recruiting ATS has AI built in rather than bolted on?**


Stardex documents AI across search, record updates, and controlled actions, but it is not the only platform with substantive embedded capabilities. Recruiterflow’s AIRA agents read CRM data and write back to records; Loxo documents MCP and Data Agents; Recruit CRM supports permissioned writes; and Bullhorn Amplify includes transcription-driven record updates and other recruiting actions. These are meaningful workflow capabilities, not simply text generation in a sidebar. Separate pricing packages or a chat interface do not prove underlying architecture, so ask each vendor to demonstrate retrieval, write-back, and execution.


### **Can Stardex search candidate notes, emails, and call transcripts?**


Yes—Stardex documents semantic search across candidate records, notes, emails, and transcripts, allowing recruiters to look beyond structured profile fields when researching a search. That scope matters when relevant experience or preferences appear in a conversation rather than a candidate’s current title or résumé. It does not establish perfect retrieval of every historical item, so test representative searches against the information actually available in your workspace. During a demonstration, ask us to show how results connect to their underlying records and check coverage for your own communication history.


### **How does Stardex turn call transcripts into candidate-record updates?**


Stardex documents meeting capture and transcript-based field updates as distinct capabilities: AI Notetaker captures conversations, while the Starter plan separately lists AI field updates from transcripts. Notetaker connects to Google or Microsoft calendars, joins eligible Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams meetings, and associates recordings, transcripts, and summaries with attendee records. Administrators and users control enablement, calendars, and meeting exclusions, but those capture controls should not be confused with field-update approval settings. Ask us to demonstrate the transcript-to-field workflow and confirm which fields your team intends to maintain.


### **Does Stardex Profile Refresh require credits?**


Yes—Stardex Profile Refresh uses purchased refresh credits to check selected candidate and contact records against multiple data providers on a configurable cadence. It retrieves available changes in company, title, and work history, making it scheduled, provider-dependent enrichment rather than guaranteed real-time detection of every job change. Agencies should decide which records warrant ongoing refresh and confirm credit allowances and purchase terms before estimating recurring costs. Ask us to demonstrate record selection and scheduling, then assess whether the available provider coverage fits the candidate markets your firm serves.


### **Do Loxo and Recruit CRM also support MCP?**


Yes—Loxo and Recruit CRM also document MCP, so agent access is not exclusive to Stardex. Loxo documents connections to tools including Claude and ChatGPT, while Recruit CRM documents contact enrichment, activity creation and updates, and granular role-level read/write permissions under the connected user’s identity. Stardex’s remote MCP server supports recruiting-entity searches and controlled writes, subject to available tools, authenticated-user permissions, and compatible client approval behavior. Compare the specific tools and permission controls each vendor documents, and follow our recommendation to test read-only lookups before enabling updates.


### **What should agencies verify about AI credits, plan restrictions, and total cost?**


Agencies should separate base subscriptions, AI-plan restrictions, enrichment or refresh credits, per-run usage, and billing terms before comparing total cost. Stardex lists transcript-based field updates in Starter, while Profile Refresh uses purchased credits; Recruiterflow separates its AIRA offering and documents per-run agent credits. Recruit CRM gates MCP to Business and above and identifies several credit-consuming features. Confirm allowances, overages, contract terms, and monthly versus annual billing directly before calculating a comparable budget.
